identity.title: Resolved Millimeter Observations of the HR 8799 Debris Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present 1.3 millimeter observations of the debris disk surrounding the HR 8799 multi-planet system from the Submillimeter Array to complement archival ALMA observations that spatially filtered away the bulk of the emission.

evidence.quote: The phase center was set at $\alpha=23^\text{h}07^\text{m}28.72$, $\delta=+21\ensuremath{^\circ}08\ensuremath{'}03.3\ensuremath{''}$ (J2000)

question.value: What are the structure of the HR 8799 millimeter debris belt (inner edge, width, geometry), the implied mass of planet b, and the millimeter spectral index and grain size distribution?

evidence.quote: To better determine the properties of the cold belt of planetesimals in the HR 8799 system, we used the SMA to obtain new observations at 1.3 millimeters wavelength
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00482.S.

evidence.quote: We retrieved observations of HR 8799 from the ALMA archive that were made in Band 6 in 2015 January.

method.value: Naturally weighted clean images of SMA, ALMA and combined data with taper

evidence.quote: These images were obtained with natural weighting, and those including SMA data use a $4\ensuremath{''}$ FWHM Gaussian taper

analysis_steps.goal: Fit parametric belt model to visibilities

method.value: Power-law thin belt with background point source, sampled with vissample, chi2 likelihood, emcee MCMC

evidence.quote: we calculate synthetic visibilities using `vissample`, a python package for visibility sampling that improves on the sampling and interpolation of the `uvmodel` task
We explore the posterior with 50,000 iterations ($100$ walkers and $5,000$ steps each)

assumptions.value: Axisymmetric geometrically thin belt, radial power-law surface brightness

evidence.quote: we make the simple assumption that the structure can be represented by an axisymmetric and geometrically thin belt

fitting.value: Uniform priors for SMA (0<Rin<Rout, F>0, -3<x<3); ALMA alone requires Gaussian flux prior 3.0-4.0 mJy and logistic Rout prior; lnL=-chi2/2

evidence.quote: we adopt uniform priors for all parameters, in particular $0<R_\text{in}<R_\text{out}$, $F_\text{belt}>0$, and $-3<x<3$.
check that the Gelman-Rubin statistic (cite: gelman14) is $\hat{R}<1.1$ for all parameters to ensure convergence

method.value: Circular aperture photometry in CASA with disk diameter from model; noise from ten random apertures

evidence.quote: We determine the uncertainty by measuring the flux density in the same circular aperture at ten random locations in the image and taking the average.

analysis_steps.goal: Convert inner edge to planet b mass

method.value: Pearce & Wyatt formula Rin = a + 5a(Mpl/3M*)^(1/3) applied to Rin posterior

evidence.quote: $R_\text{in} = a_\text{pl}+5a_\text{pl}(M_\text{pl}/3M_{*})^{1/3}$, taken in the limit of zero eccentricity

assumptions.value: a_pl=68 AU, M*=1.56 Msun, planet b truncates belt

evidence.quote: we adopt the planet semi-major axis $a_\text{pl}=68$ AU and stellar mass $M_* = 1.56$ M$_{\odot}$

analysis_steps.goal: Spectral index and grain size slope

method.value: alpha_mm from 1.3 and 9 mm fluxes; q=(alpha_mm-alpha_Pl)/beta_s+3

evidence.quote: $q = (\alpha_\text{mm}-\alpha_\text{Pl})/\beta_s +3$
$\alpha_\text{Pl}$ is the spectral index of the Planck function, $1.92\pm0.10$

we calculate synthetic visibilities using `vissample`

$\alpha_\text{mm} = 2.41\pm0.17$

findings_qualitative.value: No significant azimuthal asymmetries in residuals; 13CO emission shows no rotation signature and is likely cloud-related

evidence.quote: the imaged residuals reveal no significant azimuthal brightness asymmetries

claims.hypothesis: Is the mm belt broad and consistent with planet orbital geometry?
claims.experiment: Fit belt model to combined SMA+ALMA visibilities
claims.result: Rin=104 AU, Rout=361 AU, i=32.8, PA=35.6
claims.finding: Broad belt compatible with coplanarity with planets within large uncertainties

evidence.quote: they are consistent with a coplanar configuration of the disk and planetary orbits within the (still large) mutual uncertainties.

claims.hypothesis: Can planet b truncate the belt inner edge?
claims.experiment: Translate Rin posterior to mass via chaotic zone formula
claims.finding: No need for an additional outer planet; consistent with hot-start models

evidence.quote: there is no need to posit the presence of an additional unseen planet orbiting beyond planet b

claims.hypothesis: Is the grain size distribution consistent with a collisional cascade?
claims.experiment: Spectral index from SMA+ALMA and VLA fluxes

evidence.quote: indicates a power-law index of the grain size distribution $q=3.27\pm0.10$, close to predictions for a classical collisional cascade.

why_this_data.value: SMA short baselines needed to recover large-scale emission missed by ALMA

evidence.quote: sensitive to larger angular scales than the previous millimeter interferometer studies

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Image-based fitting for VLA rejected because of difficulty choosing a function for the visibilities

evidence.quote: We adopt this image-based approach instead of fitting to the millimeter visibilities due to the difficulty in selecting a function

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA alone gives no constraint on Rout and flux without strong priors; planet mass uncertainties are large; VLA detection ~3 sigma

evidence.quote: we must impose strong priors on both $R_\text{out}$ and $F_\text{tot}$

referee_caveats_inferred: Planet mass depends on a single assumed truncation formula and circular orbit
Spectral index relies on a ~3 sigma VLA flux and an assumed 39.7 K dust temperature
Simple power-law belt may not capture the structure; SMA flux partly in extended cloud confusion
